title: Preparation data for separating two closed boundaries, [stacks-project]
statement:
Let $X$ be qcqs, let $U\subseteq X$ be quasi-compact open, and let
$Z_i=V(\mathcal I_i)\hookrightarrow X$ be finite-presentation closed
immersions with $Z_1\cap Z_2\cap U=\varnothing$. Put
$Z=V(\mathcal I_1\mathcal I_2)$, $U_Z=Z\times_XU$, and
$P_i=Z_i\times_XU$. The two closed subschemes $P_i$ are the disjoint
open-and-closed components of $U_Z=P_1\amalg P_2$. There is a finite
presentation closed center $C\hookrightarrow Z$, disjoint from $U_Z$, such
that the blow-up $Z' = \operatorname{Bl}_C(Z)\to Z$ is $U_Z$-admissible
and the strict transforms of $Z_1$ and $Z_2$ in $Z'$ are disjoint.

proof.text: First check the scheme structures in the asserted decomposition. At a point of $U$, the disjointness hypothesis means at least one of $\mathcal I_1,\mathcal I_2$ is the unit ideal on a neighbourhood: their vanishing loci are disjoint there, and [lemma-nagata-ideal-unit-off-support] applies. Where $\mathcal I_2=\mathcal O$, the equality $\mathcal I_1\mathcal I_2=\mathcal I_1$ identifies $Z$ with $Z_1$ as closed subschemes; where $\mathcal I_1=\mathcal O$, it identifies $Z$ with $Z_2$. Where both are units, $Z$ is empty. These identifications are induced by the quotient maps, hence agree on restrictions. They identify $P_i$ with complementary open-and-closed subschemes of $U_Z$ and give $U_Z=P_1\amalg P_2$ scheme-theoretically, including when either piece is empty.

source.place: statement, decomposition clause; explicit quotient-ideal verification

proof.text: The closed subscheme $Z$ is qcqs: restrict a finite affine cover of $X$ to its closed subscheme $Z$; these restrictions are spectra of quotient rings, and pairwise intersections are closed subsets of the corresponding quasi-compact intersections in $X$. Those intersections are quasi-compact by [pqf-lem-qs-intersection-qc]. Now let $W,W'\subseteq Z$ be quasi-compact opens. The sets $Z\cap A$, $A\subseteq X$ affine open, form a basis of $Z$, so $W$ and $W'$ are finite unions of such sets, and $W\cap W'$ is a finite union of sets $Z\cap(A\cap A')$; each is closed in $A\cap A'$, quasi-compact by [pqf-lem-qs-intersection-qc], hence quasi-compact. So $Z$ is quasi-separated. Likewise $U_Z$ is a closed subspace of the quasi-compact scheme $U$, so is quasi-compact. Each $P_i$ is closed in $U_Z$, hence quasi-compact, and is open in $Z$ by step 1. Apply [lemma-nagata-qc-open-complement-ideal-exists] on $Z$ to each $P_i$, obtaining finite-type quasi-coherent ideals $K_i$ with $V(K_i)=Z\setminus P_i$.

The product $K_1K_2$ is finite type (local products of finite generating sets generate it), and $V(K_1K_2)=V(K_1)\cup V(K_2)=Z$ since $P_1\cap P_2=\varnothing$. By [lemma-nagata-finite-type-nil-ideal-nilpotent], choose $N>0$ with $(K_1K_2)^N=0$. Replace each $K_i$ by $K_i^N$. Finite products of generators again show finite type, $V(K_i^N)=V(K_i)$ since prime ideals are radical, and commutativity gives $K_1^NK_2^N=(K_1K_2)^N=0$. Henceforth $K_1K_2=0$ and the same vanishing-set identities hold. No assertion that the ideals vanish at the boundary stalks is needed.

Put $J=K_1+K_2$ and $C=V(J)\hookrightarrow Z$. The union of local finite generating sets generates $J$, so it is finite type, and $V(J)=V(K_1)\cap V(K_2)=Z\setminus(P_1\cup P_2)=Z\setminus U_Z$. On an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq Z$, $\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}A,J)$ is a finitely generated ideal by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine](a); writing it as $(c_1,\ldots,c_r)$ exhibits the center as $\operatorname{Spec}(A/(c_1,\ldots,c_r))$; this is a finite presentation closed immersion. Indeed it has that explicit finite algebra presentation and is affine, hence quasi-compact and separated. By [lemma-nagata-ideal-unit-off-support], $K_i|_{P_i}=\mathcal O_{P_i}$ and $J|_{U_Z}=\mathcal O_{U_Z}$. The relation $K_1K_2=0$ then gives $K_2|_{P_1}=0$ and $K_1|_{P_2}=0$. Let $b:Z'=\operatorname{Bl}_J(Z)\to Z$. The open immersion $U_Z\hookrightarrow Z$ is quasi-compact: for an affine open $A\subseteq Z$, $A\cap U_Z$ is quasi-compact by [pqf-lem-qs-intersection-qc], $Z$ being quasi-separated (step 2) and $U_Z$ quasi-compact. This ideal and its unit restriction give a $U_Z$-admissible blow-up datum by [def-nagata-admissible-blowup]; [thm-nagata-global-blowup-complement] identifies $b^{-1}(U_Z)\to U_Z$ with an isomorphism.

The global blow-up is glued from the local models $\operatorname{Bl}_{J_V}(V)$ over the affine opens $V$ of the affine cover used in its glue datum, by [def-nagata-global-blowup] and [def-nagata-global-blowup-local-model]; so $b^{-1}(V)$ is that local model. Fix such $V=\operatorname{Spec}A$. By [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine](a), $\Gamma(V,K_1)$ and $\Gamma(V,K_2)$ are finitely generated; choose finite generating families $a_\alpha$ and $b_\beta$. Since $\Gamma(V,-)$ is exact on quasi-coherent sheaves of the affine $V$, $\Gamma(V,J)=\Gamma(V,K_1)+\Gamma(V,K_2)$ is generated by the finite family $(a_\alpha,b_\beta)$. By [prop-nagata-affine-blowup-chart-cover], $b^{-1}(V)$ is covered by the charts $\operatorname{Spec}A[J/a_\alpha]$ and $\operatorname{Spec}A[J/b_\beta]$. On an $a_\alpha$-chart multiplication by $a_\alpha$ is injective by [lemma-nagata-chart-generator-regular]. Since $a_\alpha K_2=0$, the extended ideal $K_2\mathcal O_{Z'}$ is zero there. On a $b_\beta$-chart the extended ideal $K_1\mathcal O_{Z'}$ is zero for the same reason. Moreover [lemma-nagata-chart-extended-ideal-principal] says that $J\mathcal O_{Z'}$ is generated on each chart by its designated generator.

Define $Z'_1$ to be the union of all the $a$-charts of step 5 over all affine opens $V$ of that cover, and $Z'_2$ the union of all the $b$-charts. They are global opens and cover $Z'$. They are disjoint, even for charts from different base affine opens: at a purported common point $z'$, the extended ideal $K_1$ is zero by the $b$-chart calculation, so the $a$-chart generator has zero germ. But multiplication by that germ is injective. To check the last assertion after localization, if $a(r/s)=0$, some element $t$ inverted at $z'$ satisfies $tar=0$ before localization, hence $tr=0$ by regularity of $a$, and $r/s=0$. A zero element cannot act injectively on the nonzero local ring at a scheme point. This contradiction proves disjointness. Each $Z'_i$ is therefore also closed. Finally $b^{-1}(P_1)$ misses every $b$-chart, since $K_1$ is the unit ideal over $P_1$ and zero on those charts; likewise $b^{-1}(P_2)$ misses every $a$-chart. Thus $b^{-1}(P_i)\subseteq Z'_i$.

Since $Z\setminus C=U_Z$, [def-nagata-strict-transform] defines the strict transform of $Z_i\to Z$ as the scheme-theoretic closure of its part over $U_Z$ in $B_i=Z_i\times_ZZ'$. By step 6 that part factors through $B_i\times_{Z'}Z'_i$. This is a closed subscheme of $B_i$: the inverse image of a clopen subscheme is clopen and its complementary component has the zero structure sheaf. By [lemma-nagata-scheme-theoretic-closure-minimal], the scheme-theoretic closure also factors through this closed subscheme. Its image in $Z'$ is consequently contained in $Z'_i$. The disjointness $Z'_1\cap Z'_2=\varnothing$ proves disjointness of the two strict transforms, with their full scheme structures.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $X$ be qcqs, let $U\subseteq X$ be quasi-compact open, and let
$Z_i=V(\mathcal I_i)\hookrightarrow X$ be finite-presentation closed
immersions with $Z_1\cap Z_2\cap U=\varnothing$. Put
$Z=V(\mathcal I_1\mathcal I_2)$, $U_Z=Z\times_XU$, and
$P_i=Z_i\times_XU$. The two closed subschemes $P_i$ are the disjoint
open-and-closed components of $U_Z=P_1\amalg P_2$. There is a finite
presentation closed center $C\hookrightarrow Z$, disjoint from $U_Z$, such
that the blow-up $Z' = \operatorname{Bl}_C(Z)\to Z$ is $U_Z$-admissible
and the strict transforms of $Z_1$ and $Z_2$ in $Z'$ are disjoint.

proof.text:
Put $K_i=\mathcal I_Z(P_i)$, the finite-type ideal whose vanishing set is
$Z\setminus P_i$ ([def-nagata-qc-open-complement-ideal]). Since
$P_1$ and $P_2$ are disjoint, $V(K_1K_2)=Z$; finite type and
quasi-compactness therefore give $N>0$ with $(K_1K_2)^N=0$ by
[lemma-nagata-finite-type-nil-ideal-nilpotent]. The restrictions of
both $K_i$ to the quasi-compact closed boundary $Z\setminus U_Z$ are finite
type nil ideals, so enlarge $N$ until those restrictions are also killed by
the $N$th power. Replace $K_i$ by $K_i^N$; their vanishing sets are
unchanged, now $K_1K_2=0$, and both ideals vanish on $Z\setminus U_Z$. Let
$J=K_1+K_2$ and $C=V(J)$. On $U_Z=P_1\amalg P_2$, $K_1$ is the unit ideal
on $P_1$ and zero on $P_2$, while $K_2$ has the opposite behaviour. Hence
$J|_{U_Z}=\mathcal O_{U_Z}$ and $J$ vanishes on $Z\setminus U_Z$. Thus
$Z\setminus C=U_Z$ and $C\cap U_Z=\varnothing$. The closed
immersion $C\hookrightarrow Z$ is finite presentation because $J$ is finite
type.

Work on an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}(A)\subseteq Z$, with generators
$(a_\alpha)$ of $K_1$ and $(b_\beta)$ of $K_2$. The blow-up of $J$ is
covered by $A[J/a_\alpha]$ and $A[J/b_\beta]$. In
$A[J/a_\alpha]$, the element $a_\alpha$ is a nonzerodivisor by
[lemma-nagata-chart-generator-regular]; since
$a_\alpha K_2=0$, it follows that $K_2A[J/a_\alpha]=0$. Interchanging
the roles of $K_1$ and $K_2$ gives $K_1A[J/b_\beta]=0$. An
$a_\alpha$-chart and a $b_\beta$-chart have empty
intersection: on their overlap $a_\alpha b_\beta$ is both zero and a
nonzerodivisor, so the overlap ring is zero. Consequently the blow-up is a
disjoint union of the open-and-closed union $Z'_1$ of the $a_\alpha$-charts
and the open-and-closed union $Z'_2$ of the $b_\beta$-charts; the construction
is intrinsic in the extended ideals $K_i\mathcal O_{Z'}$, so these local
decompositions glue.

Over $U_Z$, the inverse image of $P_i$ lies in $Z'_i$. The strict transform
of $Z_i\to Z$ is the scheme-theoretic closure of that inverse image. Since
$Z'_i$ is closed as well as open, this closure remains in $Z'_i$. The two
strict transforms are therefore disjoint.
